claims.text: Conventional TOR-TILD EAM references insufficiently represent or sample the diverse atomic configurations of ab initio multicomponent-alloy liquids near melting.
A deep learning potential should be trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations of liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The training data should extensively sample liquid configurational diversity over 0.95–1.10 Tm.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys containing five or more principal elements.
The proposed method applies over the temperature interval 0.95–1.10 Tm.
A trained deep neural-network potential can accurately represent the interatomic forces and energies of the targeted liquid alloys.
The deep learning potential captures subtle variations among local atomic environments in the liquid.
Capturing liquid local-environment variation improves overlap between the reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap reduces mismatch along the free-energy thermodynamic-integration path relative to conventional EAM references.
The proposed potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy estimates near the melting temperature.
The anticipated improvement may fail outside the configurational scope represented in the training set.
The anticipated improvement may not extend to temperatures far from the melting point.
The estimated 50% reduction is based on trends in simpler systems and analogous data-driven approaches.
The magnitude of the improvement depends on the quality and configurational diversity of the training data.
